title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening of a definitional paragraph. It is redrafted almost verbatim on the next page, with n replaced by m (and at one stage 2n), so this page is the first draft.

The setup: fix n ≥ 3 and a regular n-gon in a real 2-dimensional vector space V, centred at the origin. Its vertex set I carries the structure of a 'combinatorial polygon', which Grothendieck notes can be expressed in several well-known equivalent ways: a cyclic adjacency relation, an n-cycle graph, or a cyclic order up to reversal.

The claim: up to isomorphism, the following three data are equivalent.
- A combinatorial n-gon I.
- A pair (V, regular polygon in V).
- A torsor under the dihedral group D_n = μ_n ⋊ Z/2Z, where Z/2Z acts on μ_n by inversion ζ ↦ ζ^{-1}.

The reason: D_n is the automorphism group of the standard structure (V_0 = C, I_0 = μ_n ⊂ C* ⊂ C). Here μ_n acts by rotations z ↦ ζz and Z/2Z acts by complex conjugation z ↦ z̄. Any object of either kind is isomorphic to the standard one. So the groupoid of such objects is equivalent to the groupoid of D_n-torsors, via the torsor Isom(standard, object).

The purpose in the context of cote 146 (Teichmüller groupoids, the 'Lego' of moduli spaces M_{g,ν}) is probably to fix a canonical, choice-free language for polygonal and dihedral structures. These presumably serve as the vertex sets of polygon decompositions or triangulations, cyclic orders at punctures, or dihedral symmetry in the genus-0 Lego. No computation or result goes beyond the definition.
errors: No mathematical error. The restriction n ≥ 3 is necessary for the automorphism group of the combinatorial polygon to be D_n: for n = 2 the combinatorial structure is degenerate (automorphism group Z/2 rather than D_2 of order 4). Grothendieck himself comments on the degenerate small case in the margin of the next page.
Implicit assumption: the regular polygon is centred at the origin of V, so that linear automorphisms preserving the vertex set form D_n. This is fine in the vector-space (not affine) setting he uses.

ideas.what: Equivalence between combinatorial n-gons, regular n-gons in a real plane, and D_n-torsors (forms of a standard object classified by torsors under its automorphism group)
ideas.modern_name: Torsor description of forms / groupoid of polygons equivalent to BD_n; dihedral group as automorphism group of a cyclic-order-up-to-reversal structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (folklore; general principle of forms and torsors, Grothendieck–Giraud descent formalism)
ideas.where_published: The general forms/torsors principle pervades SGA/Giraud; dihedral and polygon structures are mentioned informally in Esquisse d'un programme in connection with the Teichmüller tower, but not this specific paragraph

ideas.what: Standard model V_0 = C, I_0 = μ_n with D_n = μ_n ⋊ Z/2 acting by rotations and complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Dihedral group as normalizer of μ_n in O(2)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, carefully worded definition (combinatorial polygon ≅ D_n-torsor) that is the first draft of the next page. It is characteristic of Grothendieck's choice-free style but contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'L'ens[?]' is 'L'ens[emble]', i.e. the set; the superscript insertion above appears to be 'l'ens des sommets' (as on the next page) rather than 'l'un des sommets'.
The note beside (1) most likely reads 'Z/2Z opérant sur μ_n par ζ ↦ ζ^{-1}' (passage à l'inverse), consistent with the next page.
The last lines likely read 'μ_n opérant sur (V_0, I_0) par homothéties z ↦ ζz (ζ ∈ μ_n), et Z/2Z par conjugaison complexe z ↦ z̄', matching the next page.
